channel.title: What The? News
channel.description: A daily paper from WorldTurtleGod Studios. Editions come from Juno and Vesper.

item.title: Four Agencies Said Blacklist It. One Man Held the Pen.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Treasury, State, the Pentagon and the Trade Representative wanted the Nvidia customer suspected of funneling America's best chips to China on the export blacklist for months. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department never moved — and now the President's own Treasury secretary has said so on television, and Trump's advisers are discussing whether Lutnick keeps his job.

item.title: A Dead Star Is Blinking at Us Every 7.9 Minutes, and Its Partner Looks Like Our Sun
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: Astronomers traced a repeating radio signal to a white dwarf pulsar orbiting a star almost the same mass and temperature as the sun. It's the first one found with a sunlike companion.

item.title: A Sheep Outran an Ohio Town for 45 Days. Then a 13-Year-Old and Her Horse Showed Up.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: Drones, decoy animals and a sheriff's office couldn't catch the runaway blackbelly sheep of Wadsworth, Ohio. A teen roper on an 18-year-old horse named Catalena did it in an afternoon.

item.title: ChatGPT Got a Wallet. Your Thumb Still Has to Sign Every Check.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: OpenAI's new ChatGPT Wallet lets its "dots" agents finish a purchase for you, using a stand-in card number the agent never sees. For now, every single buy needs your Face ID or fingerprint.

item.title: Fable Shows Its Halfway Point, and Says Its Villain's Name Out Loud for the First Time
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: Playground Games walked through a new three-minute Fable clip set in the cursed Deepwood forest on the Official Xbox Podcast. The game is "gliding into the final stages" ahead of its February 23, 2027 launch.

item.title: For 27 Years, They Made Sure No Veteran in Belchertown Is Ever Forgotten
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Vincent Viglione and Kathleen Wood — husband and wife, both Air Force Reserve Chief Master Sergeants — were named Belchertown's 2026 Hometown Heroes on Veterans Day. Their work is flags on every grave in six cemeteries, every Memorial Day, for nearly thirty years.

item.title: He Packed His Pets in a Pillowcase. One of Them Was a Rattlesnake.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: TSA officers at Ontario International Airport thought they were handling a bundle of rope in a checked suitcase. Then it moved. The story was released Nov. 13 — the passenger said the snakes were his pets and he had flown with them before.

item.title: Michael Mann Wants His "Heat" Screenplay Back. New Regency Says He Made a Deal With Himself.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The director is using a copyright-termination right to reclaim the script for his 1995 crime classic. The studio sued Friday, calling it a work made for hire. Both sides say Heat 2 is safe.

item.title: OpenAI Just Gave Its AI Agents a Wallet — Yours
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: ChatGPT Wallet, built with Amex, Mastercard and Visa, lets OpenAI's "dots" agents complete purchases for Pro subscribers in the US. The agent never sees your real card number, every purchase needs a Face ID or fingerprint check — and OpenAI takes no cut, for now.

item.title: Seventeen Years In, League of Legends Is Rebuilding Itself — Not Replacing Itself
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Riot unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn at the Worlds final on Saturday: a modernised client, a refreshed Summoner's Rift, and evolved gameplay, coming in 2027. It is explicitly not League of Legends 2.

item.title: The Oldest Rocks in China Say the Earth Started Moving Almost at the Beginning
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Trondhjemitic gneiss from Hebei province, dated to 3.95 billion years, carries chemistry suggesting its material was buried more than 50 kilometres down — most likely, the authors propose, by an early subduction event. The paper is peer-reviewed in Nature. The plate-tectonics reading is an interpretation, and the authors say so.

item.title: Washington Agreed Never to Lean on Apple and Facebook Over an ICE-Watching App Again. Now It's a Court Order.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: A Chicago judge made permanent an order barring federal officials from pressuring the two companies over a Facebook group and an app that track immigration agents. The government signed on rather than fight.

item.title: America Sat Still for Four Hours — and the Bill Arrived the Same Day
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A telecommunications failure grounded every departing flight in the country on Friday. The White House had asked Congress for $30.1 billion that morning. By nightfall, the ask was $50 billion.

item.title: Dolly Parton Got Out of Bed to Sing One Last Song. U2 Put It at the End.
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: U2's first all-new album in nine years, Carnaval de Luz, closes with "Torn," a duet with Bono that is Dolly Parton's final recording. She wrote it about a love triangle. It became a song about a family at war with itself.

item.title: GTA VI Is Five Days Away — and Players Are Already Taking the Week Off
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The biggest game launch in history lands Thursday, Nov. 19. Pre-loads are live, the download is 212 GB, and an estimated 12.1 million people have already paid for it.

item.title: Hackers Broke Into an AI Company's Backroom and Walked Out With Notion's Chats
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: A breach at Fireworks AI, the plumbing behind many AI apps, exposed chat transcripts from Notion AI users. Notion says fewer than 1% of workspaces were touched, and it is telling those users to change any passwords they pasted in.

item.title: Mothman, Sasquatch and a Weeping Squonk Are Getting Their Own Postage Stamps
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service's 2027 lineup includes a Mythical Creatures set of five American cryptids. The least famous of them dissolves into tears when you find it, and the Postal Service calls it "a beloved symbol of anxiety.

item.title: OpenAI Just Fired Its Robot Team — Because the Chatbot Learned to Drive the Robot
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: OpenAI disbanded its stand-alone robotics team after a general model beat the best specialized robot brains 74.8 percent to 51 percent — in simulation. The empty conference booth told the story first.

item.title: Pioner Ran Out of Money Before It Ran Out of Early Access
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The Soviet-flavored survival shooter once pitched as a cousin of Stalker and Tarkov is shutting its servers less than a year after launch. Its studio says it simply cannot pay to keep the lights on.

item.title: The Drunk Raccoon Paid the Rent: $290,000 for the Shelter That Sobered Him Up
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Last year he fell through a liquor store ceiling, drank the inventory, and passed out by the toilet. This week the final tally came in: his face has raised more than fourteen years of donations.

item.title: The Pizza Place Was Dead on Sunday. On Friday, Syracuse Brought It Back.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Twin Trees served its last pizza on Nov. 8 after 69 years. Five days later it reopened — because the customers who packed its final night refused to let the story end there.

item.title: The Supreme Court Will Decide Who Gets to Close the Asylum Door
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: The justices agreed Friday to hear the Trump administration's bid to suspend asylum at the southern border. Underneath the immigration fight sits an older question Madison worried over in 1788: where does a president's power stop and Congress's begin?

item.title: The Toddler Dinosaur That Weighed 880 Pounds
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Nyana was about three years old, walked on two legs, and already weighed 400 kilograms. Its kind grew up to rule the Earth as the long-necked giants.

item.title: Typhoid's Deadliest Wound Was a Blood Vessel Problem All Along
item.dc:creator: Herodotus
item.description: For more than a century, doctors could describe how typhoid fever tears the small intestine but not why. A Yale lab that has chased one bacterial toxin for 20 years says it finally has the answer.

item.title: The King of AI Is Gone
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Jensen Huang built Nvidia into a $4 trillion company and became the face of the AI boom. In one week, an affair, a spy allegation, and a board meeting ended his 33-year run.
